summary: Big Horn NF lookout on Lookout Mountain, Sheridan County: staffed 1921-1935 and replaced by a Black Mountain station announced in 1938; no remains described.

events.note: Earliest date in these sources: lookouts stationed on Lookout Mountain and at the Hunter ranger station during the fire hazard season.
June 1922 report: a lookout was on the peak during periods of fire danger; no other real lookouts were maintained.
The forest could not employ a man who was competent or willing to observe for the Lookout Mountain station, so no lightning-storm records were obtained.
Two men from the Tongue River CCC camp staffed the lookout from July through September.
October 1938 announcement that a new station on Black Mountain would replace the old station atop Lookout Mountain.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Lookout Mountain page dates the Casper Star-Tribune item October 22, 1938; the Black Mountain page dates the same quotation October 23, 1938. The story says October 1938.
The register gives 1939 as the year of CCC construction; the westlookouts page quotes a 1940 CCC inspection note saying the lookout was completed but not inspected. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Staffing 1921-1935 is well documented by dated quotations from forest records; the build date, design and end of the Lookout Mountain station are not in any source read. The 1922 plan named the peak near Woodrock; the FFLA coordinates (44.66019, -107.37978) were not verified. The 1938 announcement date differs by one day between the two transcriptions. Black Mountain build year differs (1939 register vs 1940 CCC inspection note); the Black Mountain tower is a different peak and is covered only as the successor. Possible next checks: Bighorn National Forest history records, Wyoming SHPO, and the Johnson County Library archive.
